DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease

The clinical picture of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, failure to pass meconium since birth, and lack of gas passage in a 2-day-old infant strongly points to a distal obstruction, specifically Hirschsprung disease. The requested rectal swab for achreaglymphocytes (used to detect ganglionic cells) was premature; the definitive next step is to request a contrast enema to evaluate for a transition zone.
